about: The prompts the DM bridge (cerase-acp) sends the assistant on its own, as opencode stores them: user messages the person never wrote.

The rule both sides apply: such a prompt opens with one line, [<what>_result: <outcome>], at the very start of the message. Every prompt that carries somebody's words starts with the [turn_meta: ...] block the bridge prepends instead, so nothing a person types can be that first line.

cerase-acp builds its prompts with bridgePromptLine() in src/bridge-prompt.ts and checks each one against 'bridge' below; the console hides them with App\Support\BridgePrompt and shows each of 'person' as the person's message, with the text in 'shown'.
This file is cerase-core's. cerase-acp carries a copy written by scripts/sync-tooling.sh and pinned in its scripts/TOOLING.sha256: edit it here, then re-sync.

bridge.name: the follow-up after an answer written as a tool call or as tags alone
bridge.text:
[reply_result: not sent]

Your last message was not sent to the person: it was tags or a tool call written out as text instead of made through the tool interface, with no words for them, so no tool ran and nothing in it happened.

The person has not seen that message; do not mention it. Continue the request from where it stopped: make any tool call through the tool interface, never as text, and end with your answer to the person in plain words.

bridge.name: the follow-up after a turn that ended with no text and no tool call
bridge.text:
[reply_result: empty]

Your last turn ended without a message to the person and without a tool call, so the person has received nothing yet.

Answer the person's last message now: make any tool call the request needs through the tool interface, and end with your answer to the person in plain words.

bridge.name: the correction after files that did not reach the person

failures.reason: the channel refused the upload: file too large
no such file in the workspace

bridge.text:
[attach_result: failed]

The file(s) below did NOT reach the person you are writing to. The upload runs after you stop writing, so this is the first you can hear of it.

- preventivo-rossi.pdf: the channel refused the upload: file too large
- listino.xlsx: no such file in the workspace

Correct the record now, in one short message in the language of the conversation: say the file did not arrive and withdraw any claim that the work was delivered. Do not claim delivery, and do not emit an attach marker in this message.
